finding_key: packages/backend/src/api/v1/documents.controller.ts::mass assignment into the `documentservice.updatedocument` sink touched by this diff: the v1 api patch forwards the raw request body as the prisma update payload, allowing arbitrary scalar columns (`workspaceid`, `authorid`, `fileid`) to be set
evidence: Verified in packages/backend/src/api/v1/documents.controller.ts (Patch handler, `@Body() body: { title?: string }` → `data: body`): the inline type literal makes the runtime metatype `Object`, which Nest's ValidationPipe skips, so `whitelist`/`forbidNonWhitelisted` from main.ts strip nothing, and the raw body reaches `DocumentService.updateDocument` → `prisma.document.update({ data: { ...data, updatedAt } })` (document.service.ts:88-102). Prisma's `update.data` is XOR<checked, unchecked>, so scalar FKs declared in schema.prisma (`workspaceId`, `authorID`, `fileId`, `type`) are accepted field names, letting a workspace-scoped caller retarget tenancy/ownership or repoint `fileId` at another tenant's blob, which document-file.controller.ts then serves after checking only the document's own workspace membership. The contrast with the explicit allow-list in document.controller.ts updateDocument is accurate; the claim correctly notes it is pre-existing rather than introduced here, and the fileId-exfil variant is bounded by needing a UUID blob id, which is why I rate it major rather than critical.
